title: TCS Beats Street Estimates as Q2 Profit Rises 15% to ₹13,884 Crore
excerpt: India's largest software exporter reported ₹73,188 crore in revenue, declared a ₹12 interim dividend, and crossed a $3 billion annualised AI revenue run-rate on two landmark transformation deals with Porsche and Best Buy.
body:
• Tata Consultancy Services posted a 14.9% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹13,884 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, beating analyst expectations of roughly ₹13,700 crore.
  • Revenue grew 11.2% year-on-year to ₹73,188 crore ($7.57 billion), marginally above the ₹731.48 billion consensus estimate compiled by LSEG, led by AI-led demand and the banking vertical.
  • What it means for shareholders: the board declared a second interim dividend of ₹12 per share, with October 14 as the record date and payment on October 30 — investors must hold the stock through the record date to qualify.
  • Annualised AI revenue reached a $3.1 billion run-rate, up 19% sequentially, and total contract value stood at $9.6 billion, anchored by a five-year Porsche AG partnership and Best Buy's India capability centre transition.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) reported second-quarter results that beat market expectations on Thursday, as India's largest software services provider converted AI-led demand into broad-based growth across its international markets and industry segments.

Consolidated net profit for the September quarter rose 14.9 per cent year-on-year to ₹13,884 crore, according to the company's statement. Revenue climbed 11.2 per cent to ₹73,188 crore, or $7.57 billion, Reuters reported — slightly above the ₹731.48 billion analysts had expected on average, per LSEG data. Results landed minutes after Indian markets closed, with TCS shares ending flat at ₹2,076 on the NSE.

Estimates Beaten, Margins Steady

The quarter's growth was led by two strategic wins the company highlighted as a new category of transformation partnerships: a five-year deal with Porsche AG — including the acquisition of MHP, Porsche's Germany-based management and IT consulting subsidiary — and an agreement to take over Best Buy's Global Capability Center in India and convert it into an AI Capability Center.

Total contract value for the quarter was $9.6 billion, marginally higher than the previous quarter and in line with brokerage expectations. Operating margin held at 24 per cent, below some broker forecasts of margin expansion. Sequentially, net profit grew 4 per cent and revenue 1.26 per cent; in constant-currency terms, revenue grew 0.5 per cent quarter-on-quarter.

"We are pleased with the broad-based growth in all our international markets and most industry segments."

— K Krithivasan, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, TCS

The company added 4,258 employees during the quarter, taking total headcount to 5,98,056. As of September 30, it had applied for 10,044 patents and been granted 5,885 — including 2,176 AI-led inventions filed and 649 granted, a signal of how central AI has become to its research agenda.

Context: AI Spending Under Scrutiny

TCS's numbers arrive at a delicate moment for global technology spending. Enterprise clients continue to pour money into AI pilots, but investors are demanding proof that the spending converts into revenue. TCS has positioned itself as the execution layer for that demand: not the model builder, but the firm that industrialises AI inside client systems, with demand for AI-native solutions and autonomous global business services still accelerating.

"AI momentum remained strong, with annualised AI revenues now exceeding $3 billion."

— Aarthi Subramanian, Executive Director, President and COO, TCS

Impact: What It Means for Investors

For investors, the headline is the dividend and the deal pipeline. The ₹12 per share second interim dividend, with an October 14 record date, puts cash directly in shareholders' hands at a time when Indian equities are under pressure — the Sensex fell over 1,000 points on Thursday as oil prices spiked above $100 a barrel and the Reserve Bank's hawkish rate stance weighed on sentiment.

TCS remains the bellwether of Indian IT, and its results set the tone for the sector's earnings season. The $9.6 billion order book and the Porsche and Best Buy wins suggest enterprise spending is holding up despite macro uncertainty, even if margin expansion remains elusive. For diaspora investors, TCS is one of the most widely held Indian blue-chips in overseas portfolios and India-focused funds; a 15 per cent profit print with growing AI revenue is a reassuring data point in an otherwise choppy week for Indian markets.

What's Next

Watch the margin line next quarter: brokers expected healthy margin growth this quarter and didn't get it, and sustained 24 per cent margins will need volume growth to do the heavy lifting. Investors will also watch whether the AI revenue run-rate keeps its 19 per cent sequential pace, and how quickly the Porsche and Best Buy partnerships convert into billed revenue.

TCS has kicked off the large-cap Indian earnings season; Infosys, HCLTech, and Wipro report in the coming days, and the read-through for the entire sector will hinge on whether they match TCS's deal momentum. The dividend record date of October 14 is the near-term milestone for shareholders.
